sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
We have only recent data for Heidelberg's garages, so there is no city trend yet. The figures below are for weekdays in August and September 2026, which falls in the university's summer break, so garages serving the university are likely quieter than in term.

Heidelberg has made the street the expensive option. The council raised on-street charges from €1.50 an hour to €2.10 in 2020 and €3.00 from 2022, as part of its climate action plan [0]. Street parking now costs €3 an hour in the centre, more than the €2.50 the city's own garages charge for the first hour [14]. Paid parking is reaching new districts too: the council has approved charging for every street space in the Bahnstadt around the clock, with no residents' permits [13]. Residents' permits themselves have been through a political back-and-forth. A planned rise to €240 was dropped in 2022 [4], a court ruling on another city's fees led to a proposal to cut the fee to €36 [5], and the fee went back to €120 in 2024 [6]. It is now set to rise in small steps to €130 by 2028 for digital applications [15]. For the Altstadt the council has agreed to keep working on a plan for 17 bollard locations to keep traffic out of the pedestrian zone [7].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
Heidelberg's new garage capacity is being built away from the old town, on former US Army sites and around the station. The city's garage company started 'Parkhaus hip' on the former Patton Barracks in 2020, with 672 car and 750 bicycle spaces [1], and opened a 365-space neighbourhood garage at Campbell Barracks in 2022 with camera-based, barrier-free entry [2]. In 2024 an underground garage opened under the new Europaplatz by the main station, with about 750 spaces, 162 of them public [9]. In our data these new garages are largely empty on weekdays: Parkhaus hip 4%, Europaplatz 12%.

In the centre, Q-Park took over a central facility in 2025 with ticketless entry by number plate [10], and the city's online guidance portal now forecasts free spaces for the time you arrive [8]. The city counted 228 public charging points at the end of 2022 and aimed to have charging within reach of most homes by 2025 [3]. Public transport was cut back slightly in 2025 to save money [12].

sections.title: Operators, location, price and use
sections.text:
Prices are flat across the city, typically €2–2.50 an hour and around €20 a day, and price explains nothing about which garages fill. The city's garage company, Stadtwerke Heidelberg Garagen, is the largest operator, with nine garages and about 2,700 spaces, but most of its capacity is in the new outer garages. It prices about 15% above its neighbours, and its garages average 20% on weekdays. PBW runs three central garages at about 38%, and E.B. Parkgaragen's Karlsplatz/Rathaus garage in the east of the old town is the busiest in the city at 66%, priced below its neighbours.

The west end of the centre, around Bismarckplatz, has plenty of room: garages within 500 m average 24%, and Q-Park's Sofienquartier there stands at 9%. The garages around the station average 12%. The fuller ones are smaller garages tied to particular destinations: the city library (50%), the ATOS clinic (45%) and the university library (42%).
